section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch20 — Professional Ethics
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher accepts a gift from a student's parent in exchange for giving that student favourable treatment during internal assessment. This violates the professional principle of:
explanation: Fair, unbiased assessment of every student regardless of personal favours is a core professional ethics principle.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch20 — Professional Ethics
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher who learns sensitive personal information about a student's family situation should:

options.option_text: Maintain confidentiality, sharing only with relevant authorities on a need-to-know basis
Discuss it openly in the staff room with all colleagues
Post about it on social media to raise awareness
Announce it to the whole class

explanation: Professional ethics require maintaining student confidentiality, sharing sensitive information only with relevant authorities when necessary.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch20 — Professional Ethics
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Teachers are often described as 'role models' for students primarily because:

options.option_text: Students observe and internalise teachers' behaviour and attitudes, not just their spoken lessons
Teachers are legally required to dress in a specific uniform
Role modelling has no real impact on student behaviour
Only sports coaches, not classroom teachers, can be role models

explanation: Consistent with Bandura's observational learning, students absorb behavioural cues from teachers they respect.
